results.binding:
The package does not bind to a `<table>` element and does not render one. It holds values and no DOM. Citations: d.ts:1078-1079 ("renders nothing, reads no document, and names no host type"); README:22 ("no DOM"); guide:7-11 ("Nothing here renders ... The table owns values; the host owns everything a person looks at"); guide:1482 (Rendering is the host's); guide:1506 (browser binding "belongs in a future `src/browser`, taking a table and an element. Nothing renders in this round").

Columns are declared as data in `TableSchema.columns`, a union discriminated on `cell` (d.ts:987, :1254-1260). Column order is presentation order (d.ts:1233). Row identity comes from `TableSchema.key`, which must name a declared column holding a non-empty string (d.ts:1234-1237). There is no default key and no key generation (guide:496-499).

A sort is requested with `table.sort.set(order | orders)` and dropped with `table.sort.remove(...)`. It is read with `sort.order(column)` and `sort.orders()` (d.ts:852-904). There is no toggle or cycle verb (d.ts:842-844).

The sorted result is read from `table.view`. It is filtered, then sorted, then paged, and recomputed on every read as frozen copies (d.ts:952-953, :1112-1117; guide:590-593, :1398-1402). `rows.rows()` keeps the store's own order and ignores sorting (d.ts:665-669; guide:1485).

Comparison rules:
- `text` is lexical. It uses the language's own string order, not a locale-aware collator (d.ts:1281; guide:288-291, :1499).
- `number` compares by magnitude, and values must be finite (d.ts:564; guide:303-304).
- `flag` sorts false before true (d.ts:438).
- `choice` follows declared order (d.ts:83).
- Dates are ISO `text`. They sort chronologically only with one offset, one precision, and normalized midnight. No calendar check is made (d.ts:151-153; guide:362-403, :1462-1471).
- An absent cell sorts before present ones in ascending order (guide:274-275, :1407-1408).
- The sort is stable. The first term decides, later terms break ties, and the store order is the final tiebreak (d.ts:906-907, :1197-1199; guide:597-600, :1403-1405).
- `CellComparator` overrides replace one column's ascending comparison, and direction is applied afterwards (d.ts:40-47; guide:486-490).

DOM reordering: none (guide:1482). Accessibility writes: none. ARIA, roles, and ids are listed as host concerns (guide:1483). Keyboard and focus are also host concerns (guide:1484).

Subscribe with `TableOptions.on` at construction or `table.emitter.on/once` afterwards (guide:964-966; d.ts:1185). Release with `emitter.off(event, originalHandler)` (emitter d.ts:127-134) or `emitter.clear(event?)` (emitter d.ts:155-161). Tear down with `table.destroy()`, which is idempotent; getters stay readable and writes raise `DESTROYED` (d.ts:1132-1139; guide:899-901).
results.events:
The package's events are `TableEventMap` (d.ts:1046-1055). They are emitted through `EmitterInterface<TableEventMap>` (d.ts:937, :1096).
- `sort`: `[orders: readonly TableOrder[]]`. Fires whenever the term list's content changes and carries the whole list (guide:945). Setting the same term twice emits nothing (guide:994-998).
- `write`: `[key]`, once per row admitted, written over, or moved (guide:943).
- `remove`: `[key]` (guide:944).
- `filter`: `[filters]` (guide:946).
- `select`: `[ReadonlySet<TableKey>]` (guide:947).
- `expand`: `[ReadonlySet<TableKey>]` (guide:948).
- `paginate`: `[page: number]` (guide:949).
- `clear`: `[]`. A `clear()` emits nothing else (d.ts:1043-1044; guide:950).

Timing and guarantees:
- Every event fires after the state it reports is committed, and only when something moved (d.ts:1031-1032; guide:938-939, :1426-1430).
- When one call announces several things, rows come first, then `select`, `expand`, `paginate` (guide:957-959).
- Payloads are owned copies (d.ts:1037-1038; guide:952-955).
- Seeded `rows` announce nothing (d.ts:1165-1166; guide:961-962).
- Emission is synchronous in registration order. Listener throws are isolated, sent to `TableOptions.error`, and swallowed silently when no handler is set (emitter d.ts:41-48, :140-143; guide:964-966).

No event is cancelable. There is no pre-commit event. No DOM `Event`/`CustomEvent` is dispatched. The catalog's cancelable `sort.vn.sorter` (catalog:60) has no counterpart in the package.
gaps: The package has no DOM binding. Nothing reads `th`, `tr`, `td`, `data value`, or `time datetime`, and nothing writes `aria-sort` or calls `moveBefore()` (d.ts:1078-1079; guide:1482-1484, :1506). The sorter must build the schema from headers, build rows from cells, map `view` keys back to `tr` elements, and reorder them itself (inference from those citations).

The package has no row identity source. `TableSchema.key` must name a declared `text`/`choice` column with a non-empty unique string, and the package refuses key generation and positional fallback (d.ts:1234-1237; guide:496-499, :1195). The sorter must supply a key per `tr`. The markup in catalog:60 names none (inference).
It cannot cancel a sort. Package events fire after commit and have no veto (d.ts:1031). A cancelable `sort.vn.sorter` must be dispatched by the sorter before it calls `sort.set` (inference).

It cannot replace the sort in one write. `sort.set` with a term for a column not yet sorted appends it after the existing terms (d.ts:867-868; guide:633-635). Single-column replacement takes `sort.remove()` then `sort.set(...)`, and each call changes the list. Inference: a listener sees two `sort` emissions, the first with `[]` (guide:945).
It cannot choose the next direction. There is no cycling verb (d.ts:842-844; guide:632-633). The sorter owns the click cycle (ascending, descending, and whether a third click clears).

It cannot write `aria-sort`. Unsorted is a missing `TableOrder` (d.ts:993). Mapping to `aria-sort` values and placing them on `th` is host work (guide:1483). The match between `'ascending'`/`'descending'` and the ARIA tokens is inference; no file states it.
Text collation is not locale-aware, and `contains` is case-sensitive (guide:288-291, :1499). Locale or numeric-aware text order needs a `CellComparator` per column (guide:449-490).

It has no temporal parsing. `time datetime` values are `text` and sort correctly only with one offset, one precision, and normalized midnight. No calendar check is made (d.ts:151-153; guide:386-403, :1462-1471). Mixed spellings need a `CellComparator`.

DOM strings need coercion. A `number` cell must be a finite number, and `matchesCell` refuses `'36'` (guide:303-304, :438). `parseRows` turns numeric strings into numbers and 'true'/'false' into booleans, nothing else, and refuses the whole payload on any fault (guide:1041-1052). An empty `data value` must be an absent key, not `''` or `null` (d.ts:968-970; guide:1049-1050).
No sortable flag exists in the schema. Every declared column sorts, and the host decides which headings offer it (d.ts:128-129; guide:263-264).

The package does not watch the DOM. Rows added or removed later must be mirrored through `rows.add`/`rows.remove`, which validate atomically and raise `KEY`/`CELL` (d.ts:671-687). Seeding is silent (d.ts:1165-1166).
Pagination: if `limit` is set, `view` is a single page (d.ts:1173; guide:775-776). A full-table sorter leaves it unset.

Teardown leaves emitter release unclear. `TableInterface.destroy` (d.ts:1132-1139) does not say whether it destroys the emitter or drops listeners. Emitter `off`/`clear`/`destroy` are separate calls (emitter d.ts:127-163).

Guide and types mostly agree. The guide's event table (guide:943) lists row moves under `write`; d.ts:1034-1035 says "the order the table wrote or removed them" and does not mention moves. On `clear`, d.ts:1043-1044 says no `remove`, `select`, or `paginate` is emitted; guide:950 adds `sort`, `filter`, and `expand`. These are additions, not conflicts. The guide's Surface row for `isTableError` shows the shape `TableError` (guide:127); d.ts:494 declares `(input: unknown): input is TableError`. This follows the guide's stated rule that a guard row shows the type it narrows to (guide:110).

results.binding:
The package binds to no element. It is a data document keyed by schema field names.

1. No DOM: README:24 says "Host-independent: no `node:*`, no DOM. Ships dual ESM+CJS builds." README:7-8 says it "neither renders nor reads input itself". guide:12-13 says "Nothing here renders, reads a keyboard, or opens a socket."
2. DOM binding is deferred to a future `src/browser`:
   - guide:1754: "Binding a schema to real elements belongs in a future `src/browser`, taking a form and an element. It is not in this round because nothing renders here yet."
   - guide:1752: Constraint-API reflection and `validity` belong to `src/browser`.
   - guide:1753: `FormData`, duplicate names, and the submitter button belong to `src/browser`.
   - The only export is "." (package.json:22-34), so no browser subpath ships.
3. Schema-first construction: `createForm(schema, options)` (d.ts:160) or `new Form(schema, options)` (d.ts:498). The form clones and freezes the schema at construction, and a later edit to the caller's schema changes nothing (d.ts:466, :501-502; guide:1646-1650).
4. Values enter only through `fill(name, value)` or `fill(record)` (d.ts:539-546). Every value is checked against its field's control first:
   - `matchesField` (d.ts:1139-1150) gates the write.
   - FIELD is thrown for an undeclared name and CONTROL for a value the control cannot hold (guide:1593-1594). Example: writing 'twelve' to a `number` field throws CONTROL (guide:1615-1619).
   - The documented binding line is `fill(name, matchesAnswer(raw) ? raw : undefined)` (d.ts:1129; guide:647-676).
   - Trim and normalize are binding work (guide:1748). Reading localized values is binding work (guide:1750).
5. Control mapping (guide:234-267):
   - A lone browser checkbox is `confirm` (boolean).
   - A multi-choice group is `checkbox` (readonly string[]).
   - A radio group is `select`.
   - A switch is `confirm`.
   - Email and URL inputs are `text` with a rule, and tel and search are `text`.
   - A range is `number` with minimum, maximum, and step.
   - `file` holds names only.
   - `SelectField` holds one `string` (d.ts:1238-1243). No control models `<select multiple>`, and duplicate names are out of scope (guide:1753). That last point is inference.
6. Baseline and `dirty`:
   - `baseline` = schema `default`s overlaid with `FormOptions.values`, fixed at construction (d.ts:759-766; guide:1184-1187).
   - `dirty` = the answers differ from `baseline`, derived on read (d.ts:473-474, :739-740, :784-785; guide:962-964).
   - A field with no default and no seed is absent from baseline, and "`undefined` is the only absence" (guide:637-640; Contract 8 guide:1673-1677).
   - Inference: filling '' into such a field makes it present, so `dirty` reads true unless the binding projects blanks to `undefined` through `matchesAnswer`. This assumes `dirty` uses the same presence-aware comparison that `extractChanges` documents (d.ts:263-265). The `dirty` doc does not state its comparison.
7. Controls added later:
   - The schema is owned and frozen (guide:1646-1650; Contract 3).
   - No method adds or removes a field. The `FormInterface` methods are field, fill, touch, invalidate, disable, enable, submit, clear, and destroy (d.ts:800-903; guide:1572-1582).
   - `fill` with a name the schema does not declare throws FIELD (guide:1593).
   - guide:1744: a changed choice list "is the host building a new schema".
   - Inference: a control inserted after construction is invisible to the form. Tracking it needs a new form, which resets `baseline`.
   - `FIELD_LIMIT` caps one schema at 512 fields (d.ts:295).
8. Runtime:
   - Node >=22.12 (README:23; package.json:81-83).
   - Host-independent with no DOM (README:24), dual ESM+CJS (README:24, :70-71).
   - Inference: it runs in a browser and in Node alike, and it does not require a DOM.
results.events:
The form announces through `emitter: EmitterInterface<FormEventMap>` (d.ts:500, :754). Listeners can be wired at construction through `FormOptions.on` (d.ts:924) or afterwards with `form.emitter.on/once` (guide:1381-1383).

Emitter behavior:
- `emit` is synchronous, in registration order, in the current tick (emitter.d.ts:41-42).
- A throwing listener is isolated and routed to `FormOptions.error: (error: unknown, event: string) => void`, and swallowed silently when no handler is set (emitter.d.ts:43-48, :91; d.ts:925).
- Release goes through `off(event, originalHandler)` (emitter.d.ts:128-134), `clear(event?)`, which drops listeners and leaves the emitter usable (emitter.d.ts:155-161), or `destroy()` (emitter.d.ts:162-163).
- `on` returns `void`, and no signal parameter exists (emitter.d.ts:118).

Event map (d.ts:696-704; guide table :1371-1379):
- `fill`: `[name: string, value: FieldValue | undefined]`.
  - Fires once per field whose answer actually moved, in the order written. `undefined` means cleared.
  - An unchanged answer suppresses the event but is still rewritten (guide:1081-1084).
  - It does not fire for answers that `clear` restores (guide:1092-1095, :1373).
- `validate`: `[errors: readonly FieldError[]]`.
  - Fires whenever the error list's content changes, after fill, invalidate, disable, enable, clear, or submit. It can fire more than once per submit (guide:1374, :1296-1298).
- `disable`: `[name: string]`. Fires once per field moved, in schema order, and not on `clear` (guide:1375).
- `enable`: `[name: string]`. Same rules as `disable` (guide:1376).
- `submit`: `[values: FormValues]`.
  - Fires only on the submit that settles the form (d.ts:693; guide:1377).
  - After it, `status` is 'settled' and every write throws SETTLED (guide:1274-1277).
- `clear`: `[]`.
  - Fires on a completed `clear()`, before any `validate` it caused. It is the whole announcement of the reset.
  - A custom-validator throw during re-evaluation resets state but emits no `clear` (guide:1378; Contract 4 guide:1655-1656).
- `abandon`: `[]`.
  - Fires on the `destroy` that abandons an unsettled form, never on a settled one (guide:1379).
  - A destroy deferred behind a settling batch emits no `abandon` (d.ts:972-977; guide:950-954).

Events that do not exist: `dirty`, `clean`, `change`, `reset`, and `beforeunload` (d.ts:696-704).

Inference: a dirty-to-clean or clean-to-dirty transition is observable only by reading `form.dirty` after `fill` and `clear`. Read `status` or listen to `submit` and `abandon` for the end states.
gaps:
Guard 1 must build each of these itself, because the package has no DOM (README:24) and no element binding (guide:1754):
- The `beforeunload` listener on `window`, its `preventDefault()` call, and the sticky-activation precondition (catalog:32, :187).
- Listening to `input`/`change` on the `data-vn-guard` form's controls and calling `fill`.
- Listening to the native `reset` event and calling `form.clear()`.
- Listening to the native `submit` event and deciding whether to call `form.submit()`.
- Reading each control's value and coercing it (`parseValue`, d.ts:1202).
- Deriving or authoring the `FormSchema` from the Bootstrap markup.
